Going from somewhere between a "I mostly just listen to whats popular, and there's a few bands I really like" and "I really like music and like to explore it but that doesn't mean I have heard everything" definition of "probably haven't heard of".

Electronic:

Phutureprimitive - Chill dubstep. For me, it hits that sweet spot where it has really cool gritty bass noises that are interesting to listen to from a production value standpoint, except that it doesn't shove it in your face, and it's really chill.

Beats Antique - Really cool exotic chill sound. Where they really shine is their stage show. They have crazy videos to go with everything. When I last saw them, they had the drummer who plays on a drumset and the other guy who does all the computer track queueing and other instruments both behind white booths, with a white backdrop, surrounded by randomly placed and sized white house shapes suspended around them. Their video projections projected onto the shape of their weird stage exactly, with the house shapes being used as actual houses with different textures, roofs, windows, etc. Really cool.

Random Rab - Similar to Beats Antique, more on the electronic side, and slightly more chill

Grimes - Everyone I've introduced this chick to has caught the Grimes bug, so that says something.

Rock:

...And You Will Know Us By The Trail Of Dead - One of my favorite band names ever. Pretty solid rock group that got a fair amount of hype at one time amongst music hipsters but was overlooked by most people.

Desaparecidos - You may have heard of Bright Eyes, but I prefer Conor Oberst's punk group.

Fear Nuttin Band - Really cool Jamaican band. Pretty heavy at times.

Machinae Supremacy - Pretty solid hard rock/metal band from Sweden. Really obvious that whoever writes the lyrics is a huge video game nerd (they have a song called Nova Prospekt, named after Half Life 2), but they don't go so nerdy that it feels like it's being shoved down your throat.

3 - Extremely hard to discover band because of a poorly thought out name. I even have trouble finding them when I need to and I have been listening to them for years. Favorite album is Wake Pig and I would recommend getting the version from your favorite pirate themed illegal music getting place because the early leaked version thats there is better than the final version thats on Spotify, in my opinion.

Kill Rhythm - Somewhat generic sounding Canadian hard rock that kind of fell prey to the fact that their singer kind of sounds like the guy from Nickelback, but something about them sticks out to me. I was really into them in high school, because MySpace, and looking back I still think their one album is fairly solid. Available on Spotify.

Metal:

Insomnium - Really solid, but not talked a lot about in the metal circles I know of.

Exmortus - Popular local band from LA-ish area of Southern California, at least when I lived there. As I like to say, they're like a band where all the members did growing up was listen to black/death/power metal and watch Yngwie Malmsteen lesson videos. Last I knew, they played with scalloped frets like Yngwie, and utilize a lot of his style, but give it a fairly solid, heavy metal thing to go around it, rather than the shitty narcissistic stuff Yngwie puts out.

Antagonist - Another SoCal local band. I used to chat with the

Sikth - Really strange and all over the place hardcore kind of band. Singer sounds like he is actually insane. Lots of crazy bass and cool guitar riffs and weird rhythms. Also a lot of really cool experimental type tracks later on in the album.

Agalloch - Some of the chillest black metal you'll ever hear. Takes a black metal inspired core, but is really creative and blissful.

Deafheaven - Shoegaze black metal, with a touch of Godspeed You! Black Emperor. Really abrasive when you first hear it, because it just sounds like a wall of guitar noise with a guy pounding on the drums and someone screaming, but if you give it a good enough chance and get used to it and start to hear the subtleties, you will appreciate it's unique genius.

Powerglove - Instrumental video game and cartoon theme cover group. Takes the themes from things that make you nostalgic and puts kickass metal and shredding guitars to it.

John 5 - Off and on guitarist for Rob Zombie and Marilyn Manson. His live solos during their shows and his solo work is where he really shines. Easily one of my favorite guitarists ever.

Shoegaze:

Slowdive - Really calm, great to listen to to chill out or drift off to sleep. Popular as far as shoegaze bands go, but unheard of by non-shoegaze people.

The Brother Kite - A little more upbeat than Slowdive, with really introspective lyrics.

Classic Rock:

Klaatu - Really hyped for a while. There were rumors circulating at the time that they were secretly The Beatles. Very strange, but cool psychedelic vibe.

The Alan Parsons Project - Known to people who were around and into music at the time, but mostly overlooked by younger people because they don't really have hit singles like most classic rock bands do. They are more well known for their concept albums

Folk/Singer-songwriter:

City & Colour - Side project from guy from Alexisonfire.

The Mountain Goats - Don't listen to this kind of music as much, so they might be more well known than I realize, but this song came up on my radio on Spotify and I fell in love with them.

Joanna Newsom - Excellent harpist. Adorable. Married to Andy Samburg. My understanding of how popular she really is is skewed because I have a friend that is absolutely obsessed with her, but she's pretty good.

Looking up there, It's really weird to say that they're "bands you probably haven't heard of" because I have listened to them so much and their names are so familiar, but I hope I did a fairly decent job of skipping the stuff I listen to that most people have heard of.
